name: GPU Memory and Buffer Construction
text:
# GPU Memory and Buffer Construction
## Overview
GPU Memory and Buffer Construction defines the mechanisms for allocating, initializing, and managing GPU-accessible memory resources (textures, buffers, framebuffers) required to store and render volumetric data [G]. It solves the problem of transferring host-side [volumetric representations](#21847-volumetric-representation.md) into device-local memory structures that shaders can efficiently sample [G]. It differs from [Volume Texture Creation](1857-volume-texture-creation.md) by focusing on the low-level resource allocation and memory management (staging [buffers, texture](#15685-texture-buffer-object-for-block-types.md) objects, framebuffers) rather than the high-level API calls for [texture generation](#2769-texture-generation.md), and from [Trilinear Volume Sampling for Texture Generation](2726-trilinear-volume-sampling-for-texture-generation.md) by handling the data layout and binding rather than the interpolation logic [G].

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Device Volume Snapshot](2246-device-volume-snapshot.md)
An immutable, [compact representation](#1349-ssvdag-node-layout-and-tagged-pointer-encoding.md) of volume data and metadata optimized for GPU consumption. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by enforcing immutability upon construction and using a shared-resource model for lightweight copying. Choose this method when efficiently transferring volume state from a mutable host-side builder to CUDA kernels without exposing internal memory layouts or risking dangling pointers.

### [GPU Data Layout](2469-gpu-data-layout.md)
Host-side C++ structures and OpenGL resource bindings required to map volumetric scalar fields, transfer functions, and rendering targets to the [GPU for raycasting](#6192-gpu-raycasting.md). It differs from [Device Volume Snapshot](2246-device-volume-snapshot.md) by focusing on the active construction and binding of mutable resources rather than creating immutable thread-safe copies. Choose this method when organizing heterogeneous data (textures, framebuffers, metadata) into a cohesive state object that the GPU mapper can access efficiently.

### [ClearView Unified Buffer Construction](2475-clearview-unified-buffer-construction.md)
A preprocessing technique that converts a hexahedral mesh (positions, connectivity, and scalar values) into four GPU-friendly texture buffers—vertices, edges, faces, and cellScalar—optimized for the [ClearView](#14255-clearview.md) [volume rendering pipeline](#1318-volume-rendering-pipeline.md). It differs from standard [volume texture creation](#1857-volume-texture-creation.md) by explicitly encoding topological connectivity (faces and edges) alongside geometric data to support fragment-based rendering passes. Choose this method when rendering hexahedral meshes where fragment-based passes require direct access to edge and face topology.

### [Volume Upload via Staging Buffer](15388-volume-upload-via-staging-buffer.md)
This method transfers dense 3D volume data from host memory to GPU device-local memory using an intermediate staging buffer. It is distinct from [Device Volume Snapshot](2246-device-volume-snapshot.md), which captures existing device data, and [ClearView Unified Buffer Construction](2475-clearview-unified-buffer-construction.md), which may use unified memory architectures. Choose this method when populating a GPU-resident 3D texture when the underlying hardware does not support direct host-to-device memory mapping or when the data requires preparation (e.g., byte-swapping or format conversion) before upload.

### [Texture Buffer Object for Block Types](15685-texture-buffer-object-for-block-types.md)
A technique to reinterpret a buffer object as a texture using `glTexBuffer`, allowing direct memory access via texture sampling functions. It is primarily used to store block type colors or voxel data in a TBO and bind it as a texture to allow shaders to look up values based on indices stored in vertex or voxel data. This method avoids the padding waste (e.g., 3 bytes per `uint8_t` element) or manual packing required when using Shader Storage Buffer Objects (SSBO) or Uniform Buffer Objects ([UBO](#20844-uniform-buffer-object-ubo.md)) directly with small integer types. Choose this method when storing block type colors or voxel data in a TBO and binding it as a texture for shader lookups based on indices.

### GPU Texture Upload and Composition
Draws the voxel map to a GPU texture, optionally [compositing](#2436-compositing.md) with rasterized scene objects [S1, unofficial]. It dispatches compute work groups based on the resolution of `outputTexture` to render the voxel map into it [S1, unofficial]. The `outputTexture` parameter is a `GLuint` handle to the target texture that must have internal format `GL_RGBA32F`; its resolution determines the number of compute work groups dispatched [S1, unofficial]. The `rasterColorTexture` and `rasterDepthTexture` parameters are `int` handles to the color and depth buffers for rasterized objects, respectively, where `-1` disables composition [S1, unofficial]. A key pitfall is that `outputTexture` must be `GL_RGBA32F`; using a different format will cause undefined behavior or rendering failure [S1, unofficial].

### GPU Data Structure Memory Management
The new buffer allocates double the size of the existing data structure to handle the worst case where each segment is split, as the number of splits is unknown beforehand [S2]. The theoretical minimum storage is four floats per segment and two integer values per pixel, but the implementation uses double the size for safety [S2]. Data structures for all pixels are stored in one memory pool in global GPU memory. Two arrays maintain the size and offset of the respective data structure in the pool for per-pixel access [S2].

## Background
The methods described in this family are derived from various implementations of volume rendering pipelines, including OpenGL-based raycasting [S1, unofficial] and specialized mesh-based rendering techniques. The use of staging buffers for volume upload is a common pattern in Vulkan and OpenGL to handle large data transfers efficiently [G]. The ClearView technique represents a specific approach to rendering hexahedral meshes by encoding topology into textures [G].
